_: The named things of the real galaxy: the great hole at the centre, the arms and the bar, the nurseries and the clusters, the dead stars and the ones about to die, the globular clusters of the halo, and the two clouds beyond the rim. A region is described by what it lies near, and the laws of the place are bent by them; beyond their reach they are only sky.
kinds: the kinds of feature, in the code's order, with a name.

features: one row per feature: key, name (the catalogue's), kind, position as heliocentric galactic coordinates (l and b in degrees, d in kpc), radius (kpc, its extent or the range of its influence), strength (its weight in the laws, 1 is ordinary), when (years before the present of a known event) and event (what the sky did then), desc (how a people living near it would tell it), fact (what is actually known). Distances are the commonly quoted ones; a few are argued over by a factor of two.
Every term here is a technical term: a phrase a reader who never saw this project understands or can search for, never a coinage.

features.name: Sagittarius A*
features.desc: the great hole at the heart: four million suns of mass behind a veil of dust, and a sky of stars so close they blur into one light
features.fact: the supermassive black hole at the galactic centre, 4.3 million solar masses, orbited by the S-stars at a few hundred astronomical units

features.name: the Nuclear Cluster
features.desc: ten million stars packed into a few light years around the hole, old and young together, with no night anywhere
features.fact: the nuclear star cluster, about 25 million solar masses within 5 pc, with ongoing star formation despite the tides

features.name: the Central Molecular Zone
features.desc: a thick belt of cloud and fire around the centre, where stars are born by the thousand and die by the hundred
features.fact: the CMZ: 60 million solar masses of dense molecular gas within 250 pc of the centre, a tenth of the galaxy's star formation

features.name: Sagittarius B2
features.desc: the largest cloud in the galaxy, laced with alcohol and sugar: the materials of life, gathered at the one place life cannot use them
features.fact: a giant molecular cloud of about 3 million solar masses near the centre, rich in complex organic molecules

features.name: the Arches Cluster
features.desc: a knot of stars each a hundred times the Sun, none older than a few million years, all of them about to die
features.fact: the densest known cluster in the galaxy, about 150 O-type stars within a parsec, 2 to 3 million years old

features.name: the Quintuplet Cluster
features.desc: five dust-shrouded giants and their court, among them the Pistol Star, which throws off a sun's mass of gas at a time
features.fact: a young massive cluster 30 pc from the centre, home to the Pistol Star, one of the most luminous stars known

features.name: the Fermi Bubbles
features.desc: two lobes of thin fire standing above and below the centre, the breath of something that happened there a few million years ago
features.fact: twin lobes of gamma-ray emitting gas extending about 8 kpc above and below the centre, the outflow of an outburst of Sgr A* a few million years ago

features.name: the Bar
features.desc: the old red heart of the galaxy, a lozenge of ancient stars turning end over end, sweeping the space within it clear of the clouds that make new ones
features.fact: the Galactic bar, half-length about 4.5 kpc, at about 30 degrees to the Sun-centre line; old, metal-rich stars

features.name: the 3-kpc Arm
features.desc: a ring of gas streaming outward from the bar's ends, the inner shore of the disc
features.fact: the near 3-kpc arm, a gas structure at about 3.3 kpc from the centre expanding at about 50 km/s, with a far-side counterpart

features.name: the Molecular Ring
features.desc: the great belt of cloud where the arms are born, thick with nurseries and with the wrecks of what they made
features.fact: a ring-like concentration of molecular gas at 4 to 5 kpc from the centre, where the major arms attach to the bar; most of the galaxy's star formation

features.name: the Scutum Red Supergiant Clusters
features.desc: a crowd of dying red giants at the root of the great arm, each one a supernova waiting its turn
features.fact: RSGC1 to 3 near l=25, clusters containing dozens of red supergiants 10 to 20 Myr old, at the near end of the bar

features.name: Westerlund 1
features.desc: a burning city of giants in Ara, with a magnetar at its heart that should have been a black hole
features.fact: the most massive young cluster in the galaxy, about 100,000 solar masses, 4 to 5 Myr old, hosting the magnetar CXOU J164710

features.name: NGC 3603
features.desc: a compact knot of giants in Carina, bright enough to be seen across the arm
features.fact: a dense young cluster in the Carina arm, one of the most massive HII regions in the galaxy

features.name: Westerlund 2
features.desc: a young cluster still wrapped in the cloud that made it
features.fact: a young massive cluster in the Carina arm, about 2 Myr old, within the Gum 29 HII region

features.name: Terzan 5
features.desc: an ancient ball of stars lost in the dust of the bulge, older than the disc
features.fact: a globular cluster in the bulge with two stellar populations, possibly a remnant of the bulge's original building blocks

features.name: the Carina Nebula
features.desc: a bright wound in the sky of Carina, cradle of giants and of the one giant that will end it
features.fact: one of the largest HII regions in the galaxy, home to Eta Carinae and several of the most massive stars known

features.name: Eta Carinae
features.desc: a star of a hundred suns, wrapped in the cloud it threw off when it nearly died; when it dies, the arm will know
features.fact: a luminous blue variable of about 100 solar masses, which underwent a great eruption in the 1840s; expected to end as a supernova or hypernova

features.name: WR 104
features.desc: a pinwheel of dust spun by two dying giants, its axis pointed, more or less, at the Sun
features.fact: a Wolf-Rayet binary with a spiral dust plume, its rotation axis within about 30 degrees of Earth's line of sight; a gamma-ray burst candidate

features.name: the Lagoon Nebula
features.desc: a glowing shore in Sagittarius, the first of the nurseries along the road inward
features.fact: M8, a giant HII region in the Sagittarius arm, 1.25 kpc away

features.name: the Omega Nebula
features.desc: a swan of light on the inner arm, hiding a cluster of hot young stars
features.fact: M17, one of the brightest and most massive star-forming regions in the galaxy

features.name: the Eagle Nebula
features.desc: pillars of cold dust standing in a wind of starlight, with stars condensing at their tips
features.fact: M16, the Pillars of Creation, a young cluster and its parent cloud in the Sagittarius arm

features.name: W49A
features.desc: a hidden furnace on the far side of the disc, making stars faster than anywhere outside the centre
features.fact: one of the most luminous star-forming regions in the galaxy, deeply embedded, on the far side of the Sagittarius arm

features.name: W51
features.desc: a great dark cloud in Aquila lit from within
features.fact: a giant molecular cloud complex with active massive star formation, at the tangent point of the Sagittarius arm

features.name: Kepler's Supernova
features.event: A new star burns in Ophiuchus for a year, bright enough to see by day; then it fades.
features.fact: SN 1604, the last supernova seen in the galaxy, a white dwarf explosion about 5 kpc away

features.name: the Local Bubble
features.desc: a cavity of hot thin gas a few hundred light years across, blown out by the dead stars of the Scorpion; the Sun is passing through it
features.fact: a low-density region of hot ionised gas around the Sun, about 300 ly across, excavated by supernovae in the last 10 to 20 Myr

features.name: the Radcliffe Wave
features.desc: a wave of cold gas nine thousand light years long undulating through the Local arm; every nearby nursery lies along it like beads on a string
features.fact: a coherent 2.7 kpc long structure of molecular gas discovered in 2020, connecting Orion, Taurus, Perseus, Cepheus and Cygnus, oscillating through the plane

features.name: the Scorpius-Centaurus Association
features.desc: the nearest nursery of great stars, spread across a quarter of the southern sky; its dead have already reached the Sun as iron on the sea floor
features.fact: the nearest OB association, about 400 ly away, 5 to 20 Myr old; supernovae in it deposited iron-60 on Earth 2 to 3 Myr ago

features.name: the Orion Nebula
features.desc: the nearest of the great nurseries, a lit cloud below the belt of the Hunter, still making stars
features.fact: M42, the nearest massive star-forming region, about 1,350 ly away, with the Trapezium cluster at its heart

features.name: Betelgeuse
features.desc: a red giant on the Hunter's shoulder, swollen and unsteady, near the end
features.fact: a red supergiant about 550 ly away, expected to explode as a supernova within about 100,000 years; far enough to be harmless

features.name: Antares
features.desc: the red heart of the Scorpion, a dying giant with a hot blue companion
features.fact: a red supergiant about 550 ly away in the Scorpius-Centaurus association, near the end of its life

features.name: Rigel
features.desc: the Hunter's blue foot, a star of twenty suns burning through its life in a few million years
features.fact: a blue supergiant about 860 ly away, one of the most luminous stars in the local sky

features.name: Spica
features.desc: a close pair of hot stars high above the plane, the nearest star that will one day tear itself apart
features.fact: a close binary of B-type stars about 250 ly away, the primary massive enough to end as a supernova

features.name: the Pleiades
features.desc: seven sisters and their hundreds of dimmer kin, young and blue, passing through a cloud that is not theirs
features.fact: an open cluster of about 1,000 stars, 100 Myr old, 444 ly away

features.name: the Hyades
features.desc: the nearest cluster, a loose crowd in the Bull's face, already growing old and drifting apart
features.fact: the nearest open cluster, about 150 ly away, 625 Myr old

features.name: the Taurus Cloud
features.desc: a dark cloud in the Bull making small stars quietly, no giants among them
features.fact: the Taurus molecular cloud, the nearest large star-forming region, about 450 ly away, forming only low-mass stars

features.name: the Ophiuchus Cloud
features.desc: a cloud of colours near Antares, where the newest stars in the local sky are lighting
features.fact: the Rho Ophiuchi cloud complex, about 460 ly away, one of the nearest star-forming regions

features.name: the Vela Pulsar
features.event: A star dies in Vela, nine hundred light years off. For weeks it is brighter than the moon; then a spinning cinder remains, ticking.
features.desc: a spinning cinder in a torn veil of light, the newest dead star near the Sun
features.fact: a pulsar about 950 ly away, remnant of a supernova about 11,000 years ago; its remnant spans 8 degrees of sky

features.name: Geminga
features.event: A star dies in the Twins, eight hundred light years off. The sky is bright for a year; the space around the Sun is swept clear.
features.desc: a dead star in the Twins that shines only in light no eye can see
features.fact: a nearby neutron star about 800 ly away, radio-quiet, seen only in gamma rays and X-rays; its supernova may have helped shape the Local Bubble

features.name: RX J1856.5-3754
features.desc: a bare dead star drifting through the Southern Crown, the nearest of its kind, cooling in silence
features.fact: one of the Magnificent Seven isolated neutron stars, about 400 ly away, the closest known

features.name: PSR J0437-4715
features.desc: a dead star spun up by its companion until it turns a hundred times a second, the steadiest clock in the sky
features.fact: the nearest millisecond pulsar, about 510 ly away, with a white dwarf companion

features.name: the Cygnus Loop
features.event: A star dies in the Swan, two and a half thousand light years off. Its veil is still expanding.
features.desc: a torn veil of light in the Swan, the wreck of a star that died when the ice was retreating
features.fact: the Veil Nebula, a supernova remnant about 2,400 ly away, some 20,000 years old

features.name: the Monogem Ring
features.event: A star dies between the Twins and the Unicorn, a thousand light years off.
features.desc: a faint ring of old fire in the sky between the Twins and the Unicorn
features.fact: a large old supernova remnant about 1,000 ly away, associated with the pulsar PSR B0656+14

features.name: Gaia BH1
features.desc: a sun like the Sun in Ophiuchus, circling nothing: the nearest of the quiet holes
features.fact: the nearest known black hole, about 1,560 ly away, 9.6 solar masses, in a wide orbit with a Sun-like star; dormant

features.name: Gaia BH3
features.desc: an old and metal-poor star in the Eagle bound to a hole of thirty suns, a stranger from the halo passing through the disc
features.fact: a 33 solar mass dormant black hole about 1,900 ly away, the most massive stellar black hole known in the galaxy, on a halo orbit

features.name: A0620-00
features.desc: a hole in the Unicorn feeding slowly on a small star, and flaring once in a lifetime
features.fact: V616 Monocerotis, a black hole X-ray transient about 3,300 ly away, 6.6 solar masses; outbursts in 1917 and 1975

features.name: Gaia BH2
features.desc: a red giant in the Centaur in a long slow orbit around nothing
features.fact: a 9 solar mass dormant black hole about 3,800 ly away with a red giant companion in a 1,277 day orbit

features.name: Cygnus X-1
features.desc: a blue giant in the Swan being eaten by its unseen companion, screaming in X-rays as it goes
features.fact: the first black hole identified, 21 solar masses, about 7,200 ly away, accreting from a blue supergiant

features.name: V404 Cygni
features.desc: a hole in the Swan that wakes once in a generation and outshines the arm
features.fact: a black hole X-ray transient about 7,800 ly away, 9 solar masses; outbursts in 1938, 1956, 1989 and 2015

features.name: Cygnus X
features.desc: a great lit cloud along the Swan, the nearest place where giants are born by the hundred
features.fact: one of the richest star-forming complexes in the galaxy, about 4,600 ly away, containing the Cygnus OB2 association

features.name: Deneb
features.desc: the Swan's tail, a white giant so bright it is seen across the whole arm
features.fact: a blue-white supergiant about 2,600 ly away, among the most luminous stars known; its distance is uncertain

features.name: VY Canis Majoris
features.desc: a red star so swollen that it would swallow the orbits of the outer planets, shedding itself in clouds
features.fact: a red hypergiant about 3,900 ly away, one of the largest stars known, losing mass in great eruptions

features.name: the Rosette Nebula
features.desc: a wreath of lit cloud in the Unicorn around a young cluster
features.fact: a large HII region about 5,200 ly away with the open cluster NGC 2244 at its centre

features.name: the Coalsack
features.desc: a hole in the southern sky by the Cross where no stars show: a dark cloud near enough to hide them
features.fact: a dark nebula about 600 ly away, one of the most prominent in the southern sky

features.name: the Crab
features.event: A new star burns in the Bull, bright enough to see by day for weeks. Where it stood, a filament nebula grows around a dead star spinning thirty times a second.
features.desc: a filament wreck in the Bull, a young dead star at its centre spinning thirty times a second
features.fact: the remnant of SN 1054, about 6,500 ly away in the Perseus arm, powered by the Crab pulsar

features.name: Cassiopeia A
features.event: A star dies in Cassiopeia, unseen behind the dust. Its wreck is the brightest thing in the sky at radio wavelengths.
features.desc: the wreck of a star that died unseen behind the dust of the Perseus arm, loud in a light no eye sees
features.fact: the youngest known supernova remnant in the galaxy, about 11,000 ly away, from a supernova around 1680 that went unrecorded

features.name: Tycho's Supernova
features.event: A new star burns in Cassiopeia for over a year, brighter than Venus; then it fades.
features.fact: SN 1572, a white dwarf explosion about 9,000 ly away in the Perseus arm

features.name: the Double Cluster
features.desc: two young clusters side by side in Perseus, marking the near edge of the outer arm
features.fact: h and Chi Persei, two young open clusters about 7,500 ly away in the Perseus arm

features.name: SGR 1806-20
features.event: A dead star on the far side of the centre lets go of its field. For a fifth of a second it outshines the galaxy; the flash strips the day side of every world for a thousand light years.
features.desc: a dead star wound so tight with magnetism that it cracks, and each crack is a flash seen across the galaxy
features.fact: a magnetar about 28,000 ly away; its giant flare of December 2004 was the brightest event ever recorded from outside the solar system

features.name: SGR 1900+14
features.event: A magnetar in the Eagle flares. The ionosphere of every world for a thousand light years is knocked flat for a night.
features.fact: a magnetar in Aquila whose 1998 giant flare ionised Earth's upper atmosphere

features.name: SS 433
features.desc: a thing in the Eagle that fires two beams of matter at a quarter the speed of light, sweeping them around the sky like a lighthouse
features.fact: a microquasar about 18,000 ly away: a compact object with precessing relativistic jets, inside the remnant W50

features.name: GRS 1915+105
features.desc: a heavy hole in the Eagle, spinning as fast as a hole can spin, with a giant for its meal
features.fact: a 12 solar mass black hole about 28,000 ly away with a near-maximally spinning horizon, a microquasar with superluminal jets

features.name: Cygnus X-3
features.desc: a dead star and a naked giant in the Swan locked in an orbit of hours, throwing jets
features.fact: a microquasar about 24,000 ly away with a Wolf-Rayet companion in a 4.8 hour orbit

features.name: Omega Centauri
features.desc: ten million stars in a ball a hundred light years across, older than the disc, with no night at its heart and nothing there that could bear to live
features.fact: the largest globular cluster of the galaxy, about 17,000 ly away, possibly the stripped core of a dwarf galaxy; may hold an intermediate-mass black hole

features.name: 47 Tucanae
features.desc: a second great ball of ancient stars beneath the southern pole, crowded with dead stars spun to a hum
features.fact: the second brightest globular cluster, about 14,700 ly away, rich in millisecond pulsars

features.name: Messier 4
features.desc: the nearest of the ancient balls of stars, near Antares, holding a world that was old before the Sun was lit
features.fact: the nearest globular cluster, about 6,000 ly away; contains the pulsar planet PSR B1620-26 b, one of the oldest known planets

features.name: Messier 13
features.desc: the great cluster in Hercules, to which a message was once sent from Earth that will arrive in twenty-five thousand years
features.fact: a globular cluster about 22,000 ly away, target of the 1974 Arecibo message

features.name: Messier 22
features.desc: a bright ball of old stars toward the centre, with two small holes at its heart
features.fact: a globular cluster about 10,000 ly away toward the bulge, with two candidate stellar-mass black holes

features.name: NGC 6397
features.desc: a collapsed ball of old stars in Ara, its core a knot of dead stars
features.fact: one of the two nearest globular clusters, about 7,800 ly away, with a core-collapsed centre of white dwarfs and neutron stars

features.name: the Sagittarius Stream
features.desc: a river of stars wrapped around the galaxy, the remains of a small one being eaten; it has passed through the disc more than once
features.fact: the tidal stream of the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy, whose core is about 70,000 ly away on the far side of the centre; its passages through the disc may have triggered episodes of star formation

features.name: the Large Cloud
features.desc: a small galaxy hanging in the southern sky like a torn piece of the Milky Way, with a nursery in it brighter than any in the disc
features.fact: the Large Magellanic Cloud, about 160,000 ly away, home of the Tarantula Nebula and SN 1987A

features.name: the Small Cloud
features.desc: a fainter smudge beside the Large Cloud, joined to it by a bridge of gas
features.fact: the Small Magellanic Cloud, about 200,000 ly away

features.name: Andromeda
features.desc: the other great galaxy, a faint oval in the northern sky, falling toward this one across an emptiness that will take four billion years to cross
features.fact: M31, about 2.5 million ly away, on a collision course with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years
